function.mechanism: Partial acid hydrolysis reduces starch molecular size and viscosity, altering thickening/gel behavior and process performance.

adi.basis: No EFSA numerical ADI identified for E1401 in retrieved EFSA materials; E1401 appears in EFSA's 2012 call for data for re-evaluation support.

efsa.key_finding: Accessible EFSA source found was a call for technical/toxicological data including E1401; no dedicated EFSA scientific opinion for E1401 was identified in this run.

adi.basis: ADI NOT SPECIFIED (toxicological evaluation listed in 2016; 2018 entry was specifications-focused).

concerns.summary: Main concern is evidence recency/specificity: limited modern E1401-targeted human and long-term toxicology data were identified.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA toxicological monograph concluded ADI not specified and described acid-treated starches as normal food constituents.
21 CFR 172.892 permits food starch-modified for direct addition to food with defined conditions.
No IARC classification entry found for acid-treated starch/CAS 9005-84-9 in current IARC classification dataset checked.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is set by JECFA (ADI not specified), and no EFSA numeric ADI was identified; quantitative exceedance assessment was not possible from retrieved data.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory authorizations (EU/FDA), JECFA ADI not specified, and absence of IARC listing support low concern; limited modern E1401-specific toxicology prevents risk_free classification.
key_factors: EU authorization across many categories (often quantum satis)
FDA permission under 21 CFR 172.892 with conditions
